title: Continuous dequeue latency surface probe for mixed-token workloads
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a reproducible harness that quantifies how continuous batching + queueing interact under heterogeneous session mixes (short/long seqs, interactive vs. streaming). This probe focuses on the dequeue path: how queued requests get pulled into batches, how batching amplification affects p95, and where queueing creates hidden latency tails when mixed with steady background throughput. We will capture tokens/sec, per-request p50/p95/p99, queue depth histograms, and a regression sentinel that raises alerts when p95 increases significantly between runs. The harness should be usable in CI to guard against performance regressions and in perf labs for controlled experiments.
motivation: Recent incidents and benchmarking runs show non-linear p95 amplification when microbursts of long-token sessions intersect with a steady continuous batching regime. Existing probes exercise arrival shapes or batching in isolation; we need a tool that synthesizes long-short mixes, variable arrival jitter, and different dequeue thresholds to expose amplification surfaces and identify knee points for autoscaler and kernel selection heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can synthesize at least 6 canonical mixed workload profiles (bimodal short/long, heavy-interactive, background-bulk, microburst-on-steady-state, latency-critical-first, and tail-heavy).
Each profile can be replayed deterministically with configurable seed and run length (default 15m) and yields stable metrics across 3 independent runs (p95 variance < 5%).

Instrumented metrics include tokens/sec, request p50/p95/p99, queue_depth distribution, batch_size distribution, KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end dequeue time split (queue wait, batch assembly, execution).
A regression sentinel compares baseline and candidate runs and flags if p95 increases by > 10% or tokens/sec drops by > 8% for the same input mix.
Dashboard panels and PromQL/SQL queries are provided for quick triage; sample graphs load in Console perf view and link to the run artifacts.
CI job 'perf/dequeue-surface' exists and runs the light profile on every PR touching scheduler/kernels; failing the job blocks the merge when regression sentinel trips.
Runbook and short writeup with recommended knob changes (dequeue thresholds, max batch timeout, kv-prefix caching window) included for on-call and perf owners.
high_level_plan: Design workload profiles and parameterize arrival distributions (Poisson, bursty, bimodal inter-arrival) and sequence length distributions.
Implement harness runner that can drive live runtime or local simulator; support both synthetic tokens and recorded traces.
Add probes for precise dequeue timing (timestamps at enqueue, dequeue decision, batch dispatch) and capture batch composition metadata.
Create metrics exporter (Prometheus-compatible) and a small Console dashboard with comparison panels and run artifact links.
Implement regression sentinel tool that ingests two runs and emits pass/fail and a compact summary (CSV/JSON) for CI.
Run a parameter sweep to map p95 surface across dequeue timeout, max batch size, and background throughput.
detailed_steps: Week 1: Finalize profiles, extend arrival generator to support seedable bimodal and bursty patterns, write unit tests for determinism.
Week 2: Add per-request tracing hooks in runtime to record enqueue->dequeue->dispatch timings; ensure low overhead instrumentation (sampled at 1%).
Week 3: Build exporter + dashboard panels; create PromQL queries for tokens/sec and p95 by profile tag.
Week 4: Implement regression sentinel, integrate with GitHub Actions for PR-level smoke runs, and document runbook + troubleshooting steps.
Week 5: Sweep experiments, collect data, write summary with recommended defaults for dequeue timeout and autoscaler thresholds.
expected_risks: Instrumentation overhead that perturbs p95 — mitigated by sampling and offline replay mode.
Non-determinism in cloud infra causing variance — mitigate by seeding and running on isolated Dedicated nodes for baselines.
False positives in regression sentinel from minor environmental drift — mitigate by requiring failures across multiple runs and providing a manual override with annotated evidence.
notes: This probe intentionally focuses on the dequeue path (where requests wait to be pulled into a batch) rather than execution kernel performance. We expect to find saddle points where small increases in background short-session throughput cause disproportionate p95 jumps for long sessions. The outputs will inform autoscaler headroom rules and default dequeue_timeouts.

runbook: How to run: make perf-run PROFILE=latency-critical DURATION=900 SEED=42
Troubleshooting: if p95 variance is high, re-run on Dedicated node with --isolated=true and increase sample_count to 3
Interpreting results: look at p95 vs tokens/sec surface; identify knee where small token/sec increases cause >10% p95 drift
Remediation guidance: lower dequeue timeout, increase max_batch_size cap, or add short-session admission control for bursty periods
author_notes: Avoid conflating execution kernel regressions with queueing amplification. When diagnosing, first compare dequeue-stage histograms; only then look at exec-stage latencies. Store raw traces for at least 7 days to permit offline attribution.
